title: Checkout errors rising
briefing: You are on call for checkout. Orders are failing above the alert threshold. Review the evidence available at each checkpoint and choose one read-only diagnostic.

actions.label: Inspect checkout database pool metrics
actions.criteria: Use when worker logs or traces point to waits or timeouts while borrowing database connections.
actions.instructions: Open the checkout worker pool dashboard. Compare active versus maximum connections and acquisition latency before and after 14:02 UTC.

actions.label: Compare deploy and error timelines
actions.criteria: Use when a recent deploy is visible near the start of failures and component-level timing could distinguish a regression from an unrelated event.
actions.instructions: Compare the frontend release time with the first checkout failures. Break down errors by service and deployed version.

actions.label: Inspect upstream dependency health
actions.criteria: Use when evidence points to failures or increased latency on calls from checkout to a remote dependency.
actions.instructions: Open the checkout dependency dashboard and compare timeout and 5xx rates by upstream service against the previous hour.

fallback: Collect the checkout error breakdown by service and the first failing request trace, then reassess the diagnostic options.

events.text: Checkout completion failures reached 7.8% over five minutes, up from a baseline below 0.5%. The alert has no service or error-code breakdown.
Checkout frontend release web-217 completed at 14:06 UTC. The deployment marker reached the on-call timeline at 14:10 UTC. The checkout worker version stayed at worker-082.
Delayed worker logs show repeated database connection acquisition timeouts beginning at 14:02 UTC. The worker waited 2,000 ms to borrow a connection before each affected checkout request failed.

debrief.summary: A follow-up checkout trace confirmed requests spent the timeout window waiting to borrow a database connection from the checkout worker pool. The frontend release was unrelated. The first pool timeouts began four minutes before that release completed.
lessons: A generic alert can establish impact while leaving the most useful diagnostic uncertain.
Compare the time an event occurred with the time it became available to the investigator.
Use pool utilization and connection acquisition latency to confirm whether database pool pressure explains the failing requests.
